verified_facts.fact: UK SOC 2020 has 9 major, 26 sub-major, 104 minor and 412 unit groups; SOC 2010 had 9, 25, 90 and 369
The Volume 1 structure and unit-group descriptions are downloadable as an XLSX (289.1 kB), a PDF and a ZIP; the page states OGL v3.0

ASHE Table 14 (earnings and hours worked, occupation by four-digit SOC): 2025 provisional released 23 October 2025; next release to be announced; annual estimates by sex, full-time and part-time status and four-digit SOC; the page does not state the SOC edition
From 2021 ONS moved ASHE occupation coding from SOC 2010 to SOC 2020; occupation figures in the 2025 bulletin are defined by SOC 2020

All 2025 estimates are provisional; 2024 estimates are revised; full-time means more than 30 paid hours a week (25 or more for teaching professions); median gross weekly earnings for full-time employees were 766.60 GBP in April 2025

Correction of 19 December 2025: annual earnings estimates for occupation 3312 in some local areas were in error; estimates for 3312, 331 and 33 in London, the South East, East and the UK were suppressed in Tables 2, 3, 14, 15 and 20; to be reviewed in the revised 2025 dataset (October or November 2026)

The 2018 ASHE QMI (last revised 25 October 2018) describes weekly and hourly analyses as employees on adult rates whose pay was not affected by absence, annual analyses as employees on adult rates in the same job for more than one year, coefficient of variation bands (5%, 10%, 20%), a 1% PAYE sample of about 180,000 jobs; it still says SOC 2010 and gives no symbol legend
Annual pay in the bulletin includes pay affected by absence, so annual figures are not directly comparable with weekly or hourly figures
ONS content is under OGL v3.0 except where otherwise stated; third-party photographs, illustrations and videos are outside it; no specific attribution wording is given

Structural indication only: the local V1 UK rows have 9 one-digit, 26 two-digit, 103 three-digit and 388 four-digit codes plus one row without a code.
